Thanksgiving storm knocks out power, disrupts flights on US East Coast

Strong winds of up to 70 mph caused over 400 flight cancellations and power outages affecting hundreds of thousands across the US East Coast.

NEW YORK: A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the US East Coast on Thursday (Nov 26), knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of users as wind gusts of up to 70 mph (112 kph) toppled trees and power lines. Heavy rains flooded coastal areas, while utilities warned that rain-soaked ground and strong winds could increase the risk of falling trees and power outages. Nearly 200,000 homes and businesses had no power in Virginia and another 177,000 in Maryland as of 2:26pm ET (Friday, 3.26am, Singapore time) according to poweroutage.us, which also showed Pennsylvania, New Jersey and North Carolina each had tens of thousands of utility customers without electricity . Utilities and state officials had warned the combination of strong onshore winds and rain could cause widespread power disruptions.

Wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph were reported or forecast across parts of Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and coastal New England, according to the US National Weather Service. New York City Emergency Management reported winds intensified on Thursday afternoon, reaching 56 mph (90 kph) at LaGuardia Airport. The NWS said strong onshore winds associated with the storm, combined with king tides, were causing coastal flooding in low-lying communities along portions of the East Coast.

A person holds onto their upturned umbrella while crossing the street during high winds and rain during a Thanksgiving Day storm in New York City, US, Nov 26, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Adam Gray)

The threat of storms had already led officials to postpone Thursday's 100th edition of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City, marking the first time the event has been rescheduled due to severe weather. The storm also disrupted holiday air travel, with more than 400 US flights canceled and some 1,600 delayed by early on Thursday afternoon, according to FlightAware. Major airports in the Washington and New York City areas were among the hardest hit. "A powerful coastal storm will continue to bring severe impacts to the region through today into this evening due to damaging high winds accompanied by heavy rainfall," the NWS said. "The storm departs overnight into Friday."

Source: Reuters/fs

Crew member dies after diesel tanker capsizes off Ibiza, no pollution so far

The tanker carried up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel, but authorities reported no major spill and activated Spain’s Level 2 maritime pollution response plan.

A rescue vessel moves next to the capsized oil tanker Med Emre off Ibiza, Spain, Nov 26, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/CGT Mar y Puertos)

MADRID: At least one crew member aboard a ship carrying diesel has died after the vessel capsized and partially sank off the Spanish island of Ibiza on Thursday (Nov 26), regional authorities said , adding there were no signs of pollution so far. The Malta-flagged chemical tanker Med Emre was sailing from Algeciras to Barcelona and may have been carrying up to 7,000 metric tons of diesel when it keeled over about 30 nautical miles (56 km) off Ibiza 's northwestern coast, the Balearic Islands' interior department said. Emergency services said all 17 crew members were rescued, but one died after being taken directly to Ibiza 's Can Misses hospital. Six others were brought to Ibiza airport and taken to two hospitals with light injuries, primarily hypothermia. Of the remaining crew, five were taken to Valencia and five remained in good condition aboard a rescue vessel, they added.

Pablo Garriz, the Balearic Islands' regional head of emergencies, said the crew included Turkish and Indian nationals, but he could not yet confirm the nationality of the deceased. The tanker remained partially submerged with its keel protruding above the surface, Garriz told reporters, despite initial indications that it had sunk completely. "The positive news is that the vessel is not on the seabed but remains semi-submerged at the surface, which allows salvage and containment operations," he said, adding there was currently no impact on Balearic waters or coastline and no evidence of a significant spill, although small sheens had been observed. Technical experts were assessing the vessel's stability before deciding on salvage and cargo-recovery operations, he added.

Spain's maritime rescue service sent an aircraft and a vessel specialised in oil-spill response, the Clara Campoamor, to survey the area. Three helicopters took part in the rescue, along with nearby merchant vessels. Spain's merchant marine authority activated the national maritime pollution contingency plan at level 2, the second-highest. The waters surrounding Ibiza are a habitat for sea turtles, dolphins and the Balearic shearwater, one of Europe's most threatened seabirds. The area is also home to extensive meadows of Posidonia oceanica seagrass, which plays a vital role in supporting marine biodiversity. Spain's worst maritime environmental disaster occurred in 2002, when the Bahamas-flagged tanker Prestige sank off the northwestern Galicia region, spilling tens of thousands of tons of heavy fuel oil and fouling hundreds of beaches in Spain and France. The Balearic regional government said it was gathering information on the accident and its possible consequences, including any risk of fuel pollution, before deciding on further measures.

Source: Reuters/fs

RIYADH: The Saudi - led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (Nov 26) that the Iran-aligned group had attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, a day after hitting the largest oil refinery in the kingdom. The refinery in the southwestern city of Jazan, near the Yemeni border, is designed to process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day. The coalition said it had later destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in the Yemeni port city of Hodeidah, which it said the Houthis had used in Thursday's attack on the refinery. Earlier it said that targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure would be met with a firm military response.

On Wednesday the Houthis claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and a major crude export hub, and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan. The Saudi - led coalition said it had intercepted four drones over Ras Tanura and air defences had destroyed a drone near Jeddah Islamic Port. The Houthis , who control the most populous areas of Yemen including the capital Sanaa, have launched missiles and drones at Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings since Yemen's civil war reignited in July, in a spillover from the US-Iran war. The attacks have previously temporarily disrupted some of Aramco's operations and caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh. They also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including soccer's AFC Asian Cup and the flagship FII investment conference. Fighting has intensified since the Houthis seized strategic territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast in September and advanced towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital shipping route for Gulf oil producers seeking access to the Red Sea.

ROME: Two Italians were killed in a drone attack in Kuwait on Thursday (Nov 26) that Italy and Kuwait blamed on Iran, although Tehran has denied any involvement. The two were technicians working for Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian unit of German defence group Rheinmetall, and were at an air defence surveillance station in Kuwait when it was targeted by Iranian drones, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told the Senate in Rome. "Following a powerful explosion, both of our compatriots, according to information coming from Kuwait , have died. Two other people were injured: a Pakistani national and a captain in the Kuwait i army," Tajani said. Kuwait 's Defence Ministry confirmed that the two Italians had died of their injuries, after initially reporting that four people had been wounded by falling debris when a "vital facility" was targeted in what it said was an Iranian attack. It said the other two injured were Kuwait i and Pakistani nationals and that the attack had caused material damage.

Iran's embassy in Rome also categorically denied the claims of an Iranian drone attack on a military site in Kuwait in a post on X. Tajani told Italian news agency AGI that Italy would lodge a complaint with the Iranian embassy over the incident, urging caution and saying there was no need to attack Arab countries bordering Iran that were not involved in the war. The regional conflict erupted on Feb 28 when the US and Israeli launched attacks on Iran, and it has since widened to include Iranian strikes on Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military bases. Earlier in November, Iran said it had targeted US drone and missile sites in Kuwait after the United States struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday (Nov 26) posted that he would like to see Russian leader Vladimir Putin "pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe" in the hope this could lead to a quick settlement of the war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. "I really believe this is a strong possibility - Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH," Trump said. Trump has frequently urged a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine, but on Thursday he used broader language about "territories throughout Europe" without specifying what that meant. Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine started in 2022, other countries occasionally have accused Russia of provocative behaviour. Poland, a NATO member, this week accused Russia of deliberately violating Polish airspace. Estonia recently linked an arson attack to Russia's military intelligence service.

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday (Nov 26) demanded an immediate probe into what he alleged was a deliberate decision to release "fake" growth numbers before this month's midterm elections . The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis on Wednesday revised third-quarter annualised growth up to 4.3 per cent from the advance estimate of 3.4 per cent it announced on Oct 29. Trump 's Republican Party suffered heavy losses in the Nov 3 election. "It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE," Trump said in a Truth Social post, without providing evidence. "Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation. This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error," he said. The BEA has previously said that its estimates can differ from the final numbers because advance estimates for quarterly growth lack complete source data on inventories, trade, and consumer spending on services. Last year, Trump fired a top Labour Department official, accusing her without evidence of manipulating the figures and adding to already growing concerns about the quality of economic data published by the federal government.

S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade on Wednesday (Nov 25), saying the departure and subsequent reinstatement of its CEO had exposed weaknesses in the chipmaker's management and board oversight . "We believe the long tenure of certain board members may have compromised their independence. The company's corporate governance practices may also not have kept pace with Nvidia's rapid growth and its role as a critical global technology enabler," the ratings agency said. The move comes amid a turbulent period for Nvidia's leadership. The company's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang earlier this week, days after he resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs with his direct reports as well as a Chinese businesswoman alleged by US intelligence to be Beijing's spy . Critics and lawmakers slammed the reinstatement, questioning the independence of the board, whose newly elected chair had told investors last week Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behaviour was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct.

Reinstating Huang on Monday, Nvidia omitted any mention of his affairs, saying instead the move was "based on US government input", even as an independent board committee continued its investigation into reports involving him and a suspected foreign intelligence effort. Reuters reported on Wednesday that the US Justice Department did not conduct a formal investigation into Huang before US President Donald Trump pushed for his return as CEO, according to three people familiar with the matter. Instead, it concluded that there was no evidence he had broken any laws based on ongoing investigations into two Nvidia clients, Super Micro and Megaspeed International , which are suspected of smuggling advanced microchips to China. That determination is subject to change as the probes continue.

Related:

Jensen Huang’s stunning return as Nvidia CEO: A timeline of events

NO EVIDENCE YET THAT ALICE HUANG IS A SPY Investors were largely unruffled by the S&P move, which comes with Nvidia shares down 38 per cent since Oct 6. Nvidia closed down nearly 4 per cent on Wednesday, retracing some declines after the Nasdaq 100 index briefly flirted with a 20 per cent decline from its recent high. The cost of insurance against tech companies defaulting on debts has jumped sharply in recent weeks, but the five-year CDS spread for Nvidia was little changed. Nvidia currently has an AA rating from S&P, which indicates a very strong capacity to meet financial commitments. The highest rating is AAA. The agency said it could downgrade Nvidia within the next 90 days, but expects any potential downgrade to be limited to one notch, unless investigations and other disclosures harm the company's reputation or future business prospects. Meanwhile, Moody's said on Wednesday that bringing back Huang eases near-term uncertainty around Nvidia's business execution and eliminates execution risk associated with appointing a new leader for the chipmaker. The agency said Nvidia's Aa1 rating and stable outlook remain unaffected, but added that governance and regulatory uncertainty persists.

WASHINGTON: Russia should avoid actions that expand its war in Ukraine, US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte said in a joint statement on Wednesday (Nov 26) after a meeting in Florida where they also discussed the Iran war. The meeting came after the Republican leader, who has been critical of America's Western allies, met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week in Asia, referring to each as his "friend." "We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," the leaders said in their statement. Trump's meeting with Putin triggered a backlash from domestic Democratic opponents and European allies, with the latter having pushed to be included in US-backed talks to end the war in Ukraine.

Rutte and Trump also talked about boosting defence spending and investment in the United States and across NATO, according to their statement. The war in Ukraine and US-Israeli war on Iran were the primary subjects of the talks, it added, but did not say what was discussed on Iran. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been criticised by Trump, has said Europe had to be included in peace talks. Trump has often criticised Washington's Western and democratic allies over issues such as NATO spending, trade tariffs and what he calls their inadequate support for the war on Iran.

Elon Musk, the world's richest person, said on Wednesday (Nov 25) that every child in the US will receive two shares in SpaceX, the space and AI company he runs, pledging a gift worth some US$18 billion. Musk and rival AI company Anthropic have recently laid out sharply different blueprints for sharing some of the spoils of the AI boom, amid growing public and political scrutiny of the industry. Children will receive one share from the company and one from him personally, Musk said in a brief post on X, without providing details. In a separate post, Musk said the SpaceX shares will be transferred next month.

"The share directly from me will be transferred when my lockup expires in June next year," Musk added. SpaceX said earlier on Wednesday it would contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account, adding that Musk will personally match the number of shares donated by the company. A Trump Account is a program designed to give Americans under the age of 18 a stake in the stock market and help build wealth from an early age. The White House said in October it had opened almost 70 million accounts. SpaceX shares closed at US$127.44 on Wednesday, valuing the pledge at nearly US$18 billion.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether Musk's SpaceX share donations would be linked to Trump Accounts. "What it does is build a massive, long-term retail shareholder base," said Christopher Brankin, global markets advisor at brokerage Mitrade Group. "It builds immediate market engagement and creates a massive, financially literate client pipeline for trading platforms as that generation comes of age." Musk, whose net worth is around US$824 billion, said last month he would give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in America. He held about 6.42 billion shares in the company as of June. "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Musk said in a post on X at the time. "Giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way," Musk added. Most of Musk's philanthropic efforts have been through the Musk Foundation, which reportedly holds more than US$14 billion in assets.

In October, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged a share of their SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children under the Trump initiative. Anthropic, which recently went public, said last month it was committing 5 per cent of its shares to a new fund for the "public good". It said that the initiative, worth around US$54 billion at current prices, will give it more flexibility and scale to make donations for the benefit of humanity. Other executives have also set up major, long-running philanthropy ventures. Berkshire Hathaway Chairman Emeritus Warren Buffett, one of the most prominent figures in philanthropy, is reported to have given away US$60 billion so far, with most of the rest of his roughly US$150 billion fortune slated for philanthropy too. The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has distributed more than US$100 billion since its founding in 2000, with some of that fueled by donations from Buffett.
